name: Alejandro Santo Domingo
name_chinese: 亚历杭德罗·桑托·多明戈
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Alejandro Santo Domingo, an heir to a beer fortune, sits on the board of beer giant Anheuser-Busch InBev, in which he has a roughly 1% stake.
Santo Domingo was a key negotiator in the deals that led to the 2016 merger between Anheuser-Busch InBev and SABMiller.
A Harvard grad, Santo Domingo is a senior managing director of New York-based Quadrant Capital Advisors, an investment advisory firm.
He also sits on the board of trustees of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
His father, Julio Mario Santo Domingo, had a 15% stake in SABMiller when he died in 2011, which he passed down to his sons and grandchildren.
forbes_facts: In May 2016 Santo Domingo married Lady Charlotte Wellesley, reportedly a direct descendant of the British general who vanquished Napoleon at Waterloo.
The Santo Domingo family also owns a stake in Château Pétrus, a French wine estate near Bordeaux that produces some of the world's most expensive wines.

name: Oprah Winfrey
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2003-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Oprah Winfrey transitioned her hit talk show, which ran for 25 years until 2011, into a media and business empire.
Reinvested, the profits from her show, plus profits from films like The Color Purple, Beloved and Selma (which her Harpo Productions coproduced) add up to more than an estimated $2.8 billion.
In 2011, Winfrey launched cable channel OWN. She sold most of her stake in the network to owner Warner Bros. Discovery in 2020 in exchange for shares in the company.
Her sprawling real estate portfolio includes homes in California and over a dozen properties including 2,100 acres of land in Hawaii.
forbes_facts: Winfrey overcame a tough childhood, born to a teen mother in rural Mississippi and raised without indoor plumbing.
Winfrey has focused her philanthropy on education, including supporting a girls' school in South Africa.

name: Annalisa Doris
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Annalisa Doris is the vice president of Italian bank Banca Mediolanum, which was founded by her father Ennio (d. 2021) in 1982.
She joined the firm in 1997 after graduating from the University of Milan with a political science degree.
She joined Mediolanum's board in 2015 before rising to vice president in September 2021.

name: Francesco Patarnello
forbes_bio: Francesco Patarnello cofounded Italian app developer Bending Spoons in 2013 with his three cofounders Luca Ferrari, Matteo Danieli and Luca Querella.
The four friends launched Bending Spoons after working together on an unsuccessful, earlier startup Evertale, a note-taking app.
The Bending Spoons cofounders met while studying in Copenhagen, Denmark, and would later relocate to Milan, Italy, as their new startup took off.
The Milan, Italy-based startup struck on the strategy of buying apps and companies with a loyal audience where it sees the potential to overhaul its features and pricing.
Bending Spoons was largely bootstrapped until it raised its first major funding round in 2022 and made its first takeover of Evernote in 2023.

The company last raised $270 on a $11 billion in October 2025 to help fund its takeover of AOL and Vimeo. Bending Spoons is now Italy's most valuable startup and has bought, or taken private, a string of apps and startups like Meetup, Eventbrite, and WeTransfer.

name: Stefan Wirtgen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Stefan Wirtgen is one of two billionaire brothers who inherited the family fortune from their father, Reinhard, founder of construction equipment maker Wirtgen Group.
Wirtgen group was founded in 1961 and sold to Deere & Company in 2017 for $5.2 billion.
After the sale, the brothers created Wirtgen Invest, a family office with interests in energy, real estate, healthcare, consumer goods and finance.
The investment firm has made some 700 generally passive investments, according to its website.

name: Gustavo Denegri
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Gustavo Denegri is the chairman of biotech company DiaSorin SpA; the bulk of his fortune is a 45% stake in the publicly-traded company.
In 2000, his private equity firm acquired the distressed DiaSorin from American Standard Companies and built it into a global player in diagnostics.
His first breakthrough came when his Gruppo Pro-Ind, a components firm, merged with Piaggio, owner of motor scooters Vespa and Aprilia.
He is one of few Italian businessmen to have built billion-dollar companies in more than one sector.
His firm Investimenti is run by his son Michele and has a diverse portfolio, including medical technology, real estate and TV production.
forbes_facts: Gustavo Denegri was trained as a chemist.

name: Jannie Mouton
forbes_bio: Johannes "Jannie" Mouton, also known as "Buddha Buffett," is the founder of PSG Group, a listed investment holding firm.
PSG has interests in financial services, banking, private equity, agriculture and education.
Both of his sons serve on PSG Group's board, and his son Piet Mouton is the CEO.
The 2011 book, "And Then They Fired Me," details how Mouton started PSG Group after getting fired at age 48.
He had been fired by his fellow partners at stockbroking firm Senekal, Mouton & Kitshoff, which he cofounded.

name: Martin Knauf
forbes_bio: Martin Bernhard Knauf is an heir to one of the world's leading producers of building materials and systems, Knauf Gips KG.
Based in Iphofen, Germany, the company employs more than 35,000 people around the world and has annual revenue of over $11 billion.
Its product line includes plasterboards, cement boards and insulating materials.
Knauf Gips dates to 1932, when brothers and mining engineers Alfons and Karl Knauf obtained rights to gypsum deposits in Schengen, Germany.
Their original gypsum factory, on the Moselle River in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, is still the company's production nucleus.
forbes_facts: The family's Knauf Museum, on the premises of a historical inn built in 1688 on Iphofen's market square, houses a renowned collection or ancient relief art.

name: Florian Rehm
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Florian Rehm is majority owner and chairman of the supervisory board of Mast-Jägermeister SE, a German liquor company known for its herbal ingredients.
The company, founded in 1878 as a vinegar producer, created the famous (and secretive) herbal liquor recipe in 1934.
In 1975, Sidney Frank became the U.S. distributor of Jägermeister, which gained popularity with college students.
In 2015 Mast-Jägermeister acquired Sidney Frank, and through the deal established its U.S. subsidiary.
Privately-held Mast-Jägermeister is now owned by fifth-generation family members.

name: Gerda Tschira
forbes_bio: Gerda Tschira is the widow of Klaus Tschira, the software pioneer who cofounded SAP (Systems, Applications, Products) in 1972.
She and her two billionaire sons inherited Klaus Tschira's stake in SAP when he died in 2015. Klaus retired from the company in 1998 and left its board in 2007.
His sons carry on the activities of the Klaus Tschira Foundation, which promotes learning in natural sciences, mathematics and computer science.
His sons carry on the activities of the Klaus Tschira Foundation, which promotes learning in natural sciences, mathematics and computer science.
The foundation, one of Germany's largest philanthropies, has awarded more than $740 million in cash grants and in-kind donations.

name: Tom Preston-Werner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2020); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Tom Preston-Werner cofounded software development platform GitHub in 2008.
Microsoft bought the company for $7.5 billion, all in stock, in 2018.
Preston-Werner had left the firm in 2014 in the wake of harassment allegations, which he denied.
Following an investigation, GitHub said it did not find evidence of harassment, but that it "did find evidence of mistakes and errors of judgment."
He cofounded language learning platform Chatterbug in 2016.
